Investing in tomorrow’s growth
Coal India has always planned beyond
the immediate production cycle, investing
today to strengthen the nation’s future
energy security. During FY2025-26, we
continued to expand our project pipeline,
strengthen evacuation infrastructure
and build capabilities that will support
sustained growth over the coming decade.
Coal gasification remained a strategic
priority, with Talcher Fertilisers Limited,
Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals
Limited and Coal Gas India Limited
advancing projects to convert coal into
value-added products such as fertilisers,
ammonium nitrate and synthetic natural
gas. Looking ahead, we are preparing
a broader coal gasification programme
with significant investments to drive value
addition and support import substitution.
The Company also accelerated its
entry into critical minerals through the
ongoing incorporation of overseas
holding companies in Singapore and
Chile, strategic partnerships with
domestic mining organisations, and the
allocation of a Rare Earth Elements block
in Maharashtra. Together, these initiatives
broaden our resource portfolio while
supporting India’s long-term industrial
and strategic priorities.
Advancing Research and
Innovation
Coal India’s R&D agenda gathered
momentum with the establishment of
the National Centre for Coal and Energy
Research (NaCCER), a hub-and-spoke
modelled research centre that has
shifted the Company’s focus from proof-
of-concept studies to TRL-4 and above
prototype development with scalable
industrial applications. To institutionalise
innovation, CIL also formulated a
comprehensive R&D Policy.
Strengthening industry-academia
collaboration, CIL established three
Centres of Excellence at IIT Hyderabad
(CLEANZ), IIT Madras (CSE) and IIT
(ISM) Dhanbad (IMiN). Currently, 18
R&D projects with an outlay of about
H 225 Crores are being executed
under NaCCER’s oversight, alongside
international collaborations with Ergo
Exergy (Canada), Ericsson (Sweden),
CSIRO (Australia) and the University
of Wollongong (Australia). In addition,
13 high-TRL projects involving
pilot-scale research and prototype
development, along with 11 low-TRL
projects, are underway across the
Centres of Excellence.
Expanding beyond coal
Coal will continue to anchor India’s energy
security for years to come. At the same
time, Coal India is creating new growth
platforms that build on its engineering
strengths and resource base.
Looking ahead, the Company is preparing
a broader coal gasification programme
with planned investments of around
H 50,000 Crores, creating new avenues for
value addition and import substitution.
Building the clean energy
portfolio
Coal India continues to expand its
presence across renewable energy and
emerging clean energy businesses while
maintaining its core responsibility of
supporting India’s energy security.
During FY 2025-26, the Company
commissioned a 100 MW solar power
plant in Gujarat and advanced large-
scale solar projects in Rajasthan and Uttar
Pradesh. It also secured Battery Energy
Storage System projects in Odisha and
Telangana, strengthening its presence
in next-generation power infrastructure.
Alongside these initiatives, Coal India and
Damodar Valley Corporation incorporated
a joint venture to develop a 1,600 MW
thermal power project at Chandrapura,
reflecting the Company’s balanced
approach towards conventional and
emerging energy opportunities.

Safety remains our first priority
Mining is an inherently complex business
where safety remains our foremost
priority. During FY2025-26, all producing
mines underwent comprehensive safety
audits supported by Principal Hazard
Management Plans, mine-specific Safety
Management Plans, regular inspections
and corrective actions. Safety campaigns,
toolbox talks, pre-shift interactions
and competency assessments further
reinforced a strong safety culture
across our operations.
Technology continues to strengthen our
safety framework. Integrated Command
and Control Centres are now operational
across all producing subsidiaries and NEC,
supported by AI-enabled video analytics,
CCTV surveillance, GPS-based vehicle
tracking, RFID-enabled access systems
and traffic management solutions for
real-time monitoring and faster response.
The launch of the Safety AI Analytics
Dashboard further strengthened our
ability to anticipate, monitor and manage
operational risks through predictive
insights. Together, these initiatives are
enabling safer, smarter and more resilient
mining operations across Coal India.
Investing in our people
Coal India’s achievements are built on
the strength of its people. Supporting the
scale and complexity of our operations
requires continuous capability building
across technical, managerial and
leadership roles. During FY2025-26,
over 1.02 lakh employees participated in
training programmes, accounting for more
than 6.09 lakh training man-days. Training
also extended to over 46,000 contract
workers, strengthening capabilities across
the broader workforce.
Leadership development remained a key
focus through programmes conducted
by IIM Mumbai, IIM Lucknow, IIT Bombay
and IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, complemented
by international learning initiatives,
specialised technical programmes and
structured succession planning.
Coal India was recognised as a ‘Great
Place to Work’ and featured among
India’s Best Workplaces in Manufacturing,
reflecting its continued emphasis on
employee development, workplace
culture and organisational excellence.
Recruitment also remained aligned
with future business needs through
the induction of Management Trainees,
medical professionals and specialists,
alongside lateral hiring to strengthen
renewable energy and emerging
business capabilities.
Creating value beyond mining
Coal India has always believed that
the communities around its operations
should participate in the Company’s
progress. Our CSR initiatives continue
to focus on areas that create lasting
impact, including healthcare, education,
drinking water, sanitation, livelihood
generation, skill development and
community infrastructure.
During FY 2025-26, your Company
spent H 1,016 Crores on Corporate
Social Responsibility initiatives across
the country. Programmes implemented
through Coal India and its subsidiaries
reached thousands of beneficiaries across
coal-bearing districts, strengthening
access to healthcare, quality education
and basic infrastructure.
Healthcare remained one of the largest
areas of intervention. The Company
continued to support specialised
healthcare programmes, hospitals,
mobile medical services and preventive
healthcare initiatives. The Nanha Sa Dil
programme, which provides life-saving
treatment for children with congenital
heart disease, continued to transform
young lives during the year and received
the Healthcare Initiative of the Year award.
Strategic Future Outlook
India’s development journey will continue
to require dependable and affordable
energy. Coal will remain an important
part of that journey, even as the country’s
energy mix becomes more diverse.
Coal India enters this next phase from a
position of strength. We have a strong
resource base, an expanding project
pipeline, healthy financials and a clear
strategy for future growth. Alongside
strengthening our core business, we are
creating new opportunities across coal
gasification, critical minerals, renewable
energy, battery storage and power
generation. These initiatives are gradually
broadening the Company’s growth
platform while remaining aligned with
national priorities.
The road ahead will demand greater
efficiency, faster execution and
continued investment in technology,
people and infrastructure. It will also
require us to balance energy security
with environmental responsibility and
community development.
These priorities are not competing
objectives. Together, they define the
future of responsible mining. As we move
towards our long-term production target
of around one billion Tonnes, our focus will
remain on building an organisation that
is operationally stronger, technologically
more capable and better prepared for
the changing energy landscape. Every
investment we make today is guided
by this objective.

Dear Stakeholders,
Financial Year (FY) 2025-26 marked a period of strategic
transformation for Coal India Limited. While continuing to fulfil
its critical role in ensuring India's energy security, the Company
accelerated its transition toward becoming a diversified natural
resources and energy enterprise.

public listings of subsidiary companies, expansion into
critical minerals, advancement of coal gasification projects,
strengthening of renewable energy initiatives, and continued
investment in evacuation infrastructure.

growth, the Company maintained robust operational
performance, generated strong cash flows, and continued
its track record of delivering superior shareholder returns
through consistent dividend distribution. Coal India remains
committed to balancing three strategic priorities: energy
security, sustainable growth, and long-term value creation
for stakeholders.

4.0 OUTLOOK:
CIL has envisaged coal supply target of 850.24 MT in
FY 2026-27 which is a growth of more than 14% over
the previous year’s achievement. About 79% of the total
despatch would be consumed by power sector only.
With future domestic demand in mind, CIL has revised
its coal production programme and a strategic coal
production roadmap i.e. ~1BT by FY 2029-30. This plan
entails optimising production across all CIL subsidiaries
and delineating various enabling activities necessary to
realise this ambitious target. These activities encompass
securing statutory clearances, land acquisition and
possession, ensuring rehabilitation and resettlement
(R&R), procuring equipment, and enhancing evacuation
infrastructure such as rail lines and coal handling plants.
For sustainability and growth, thrust on minimising the
environmental impact is laid for qualitative improvement
in coal production through selective mining, beneficiation
& blending, enhancing production from U/G mines and
diversifying into clean coal technologies.
CIL has planned a capital investment of H 16,500 Crores
for maintaining its volume growth in FY 2026-27 and
beyond. In addition, the company has also envisaged for
investing substantial amount in different schemes in FY
2026-27 such as development of railway infrastructure
project, solar power, Thermal Power Plants, Coal Bed
Methane (CBM), revival of fertiliser plants etc
Marketing Outlook:
The total power generation (incl. RES) in the country
grew to about 1844.5 BU clocking a growth of 0.9 %.
The coal-based generation in the country for FY 2025-26
was 1250 BU with a (-)3.7 % growth over the previous
year. The domestic coal based generation was 1174.4
BU {(-)2.3% growth over previous year}. Considering the
growth of power generation and consequential increase
in demand, the offtake target of FY 2025-26 was 900.24
MT. The demand from power sector was 668 MT against
which Coal India Limited (CIL) supplied 588.01 MT,
achieving 88% materialisation.
The coal supply to Non Regulated Sector(NRS) was 155.5
MT (7.0 % growth over previous year) which is the highest
supply to NRS in any given year.
The e-auction coal booking during FY 2025-26 was
101.72 MT against 89.38 MT during previous year. The
premium on e-auction during FY 2025-26 was 46 % as
against 48 % in previous FY.
Fuel Supply Agreement (FSA) commitment for Power
Sector, Non-Power and bridge linkage were at about
793.90 Million Tonne Per Annum (MTPA) as on
31.03.2026. The demand of CIL coal from Power sector
as per Ministry of Coal for FY 2026-27 is 669.80 MT. The
yearly target for FY 2026-27 has been set at about 850.24
MT so as to cater to the entire demand of power sector,
NRS and also to substitute the substitutable imported
coal in the country. In order to tap the potential future
market for coal consumption and explore alternative uses
of domestic coal, CIL intends to offer more coking coal
to steel sector and also supply coal for upcoming coal
gasification projects.
Mechanised and Computerised Loading
Coal India Limited (CIL) had an installed rapid loading
capacity of 151 MTPA as of August 2019. In addition to
this, CIL has undertaken significant initiatives to enhance
mechanised coal transportation and loading systems
under its First Mile Connectivity (FMC) projects. A total of
72 FMC projects have been planned to be implemented
in four phases, with an aggregate capacity of 843 MTY. As
of FY 2025–26, FMC projects with a cumulative capacity
of 432 MTY have been operationalised. Upon completion
of all FMC projects, CIL’s total mechanised/rapid loading
capacity is projected to reach 994 MTY by FY 2028–29.
The share of SILO loading is expected to grow upto 39%
in the FY 2026-27.
In order to understand the requirements of the
consumers, CIL is conducting quarterly zone-wise
consumer meeting with both power and non-power
consumers separately. Further, subsidiaries also conduct
meeting with the consumers at regular intervals. In
addition, to promote ease of doing business, CIL has
set up a Consumer Grievance Redressal Mechanism
to redress the grievances of consumers related to coal
supplies and other related issues.
Customer satisfaction through quality assurance and
transparency in business operations have been priority
areas for CIL. The initiatives taken to build Consumers’
confidence and satisfaction include supply of sized
coal as per FSA provisions, extension of third-party
sampling facility to all sectors of consumers under all
schemes through deployment of empanelled Third-Party
Agencies (TPA) as per the choice of consumer, Collection
of samples through Auto Mechanical Samplers at Silo
Loading points, Operationalisation Mechanical Augurs
for coal sample collection, providing live camera feed
to the customers for observing sample collection and
preparation process, timely issuance of credit/ debit
notes on quality grounds etc.
At present, twelve independent Third Party sampling
agencies have been empanelled. Out of these, 10
agencies have been empanelled by Power Finance
Corporation Ltd (PFCL) under Ministry of Power and 2 by
CIL to cater to both power and non-power sector, giving
consumers a wide option to choose from the empanelled
agencies. As a result of conscious and continuous
measures taken towards quality maintenance, a) The gap
between the weighted average of declared and analysed
GCV of coal based on results received for FY 2025-26 is
only 56.7 Kcal/kg which is well within the GCV band of
same Grade and b) The final grade conformity including
referee for FY 2025-26 is 86%.
Coal India Limited has significantly advanced transparency
and efficiency in its operations through the Online
Reconciliation Portal, which integrates quantity, quality,
and finance data into a unified digital framework. Widely
adopted by power sector utilities, captive power plants,
CPSEs, and non-regulated sector consumers, the portal
has facilitated over 1,600 joint reconciliation statements,
thereby reducing disputes and strengthening consumer
confidence. By offering a comprehensive suite of
services—including customer profiles, contracts, payment
tracking, railway receipt details, and invoice records in
downloadable formats—the platform has streamlined
settlements and provided a one-stop solution for
stakeholders. This digital transformation has enhanced
ease of doing business and reinforced CIL’s commitment
to accountability and operational excellence.

1. Introduction
Coal India Limited (CIL), as the largest coal mining
company and a key national energy asset, has been
taking extensive steps to diversify into renewable
energy in alignment with India's clean energy
transition. CIL's initiatives support the national
target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based
capacity by 2030 and contribute substantially to
reducing the carbon footprint of government-owned
industrial infrastructure. This note summarises the
status, progress, and direction of CIL's renewable
energy initiatives.
2. PM Surya Ghar Yojna - Rooftop Solar Implementation
across CIL
Coal India Limited (CIL) has successfully achieved
complete saturation of rooftop solar installations
across eligible administrative, residential, and
operational buildings of CIL and its subsidiaries
under the PM Surya Ghar Yojana. A total rooftop
solar capacity of 35.19 MW has been installed. The
achievement reflects CIL's proactive contribution
towards promotion of renewable energy and
advancement of the Government of India's
sustainability and energy transition goals.
3. Solar Energy Expansion - Ground-Mounted and
Utility-Scale Projects
Solar power deployment forms the core of CIL's
renewable energy diversification strategy. CIL
aims to develop significant solar capacity through
multiple implementation routes. The company has
committed to achieving 3,000 MW of solar capacity
by FY 2027-28 as part of its internal net-zero target.
This planned capacity addition will subsequently
scale-up to 9,500 MW by FY 2029-30.
To meet these targets, CIL is adopting a blended
development strategy that includes joint ventures
with state generating companies, tariff-based
competitive bidding for sale of power through
PPA, captive projects on own land for internal
consumption, and projects developed for
commercial and industrial (C&I) consumers. Till date
CIL has an installed capacity of 357.65 MW and
projects of around 523.50 MW are under execution
and expected to be completed by FY 26-27.
Major partnerships with Rajasthan Vidyut Utpadan
Nigam Limited (RVUNL) and Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut
Utpadan Nigam Limited (UPRVUNL) are central to
CIL's multi- gigawatt solar rollout. Concurrently, CIL
also developing solar capacity at Khavda, Gujarat and
multiple subsidiary locations.
4. Major Ongoing Renewable Energy Projects of CIL
In Gujarat, CIL is progressing with a 300 MW solar
project in the Khavda renewable energy park. Across
subsidiaries, a robust pipeline of ground-mounted
and rooftop projects is being implemented,
including 223.50 MW currently under construction
and around 344.25 MW under DPR or feasibility
assessment. These projects span BCCL, CCL, ECL,
MCL, NCL, SECL, and WCL, demonstrating sustained
investment across coalfields.
CIL is also exploring hybrid solar-wind-BESS to
expand its capacity pipeline. Already CIL has signed
BESPA for 187.5 MW/750 MWh (TGGENCO) and
for 80 MW/320 MWh (GRIDCO). Also, CIL has won
TBCB tender of NHPC for MW Solar Project at Jalaun
Solar Park, UP.
5. Wind Energy Programme
CIL has initiated looping wind energy portfolio
in wind-rich regions i.e. Rajasthan, Gujarat, and
Andhra Pradesh.
